bms_g_4168_20000690.name: bms_rtc_lse_selected
bms_g_4168_20000690.description: RTC clock-source flag. 1 when the RTC is started from the LSE crystal (32.768 kHz), 0 when it runs from the LSI RC oscillator. Written by bms_rtc_clock_bringup and bms_rtc_select_lse_and_start (1 once LSE is in use, probably), cleared to 0 by bms_rtc_fallback_lsi_start and by bms_rtc_hal_init when HAL_RTC_Init fails. bms_rtc_hal_init picks the asynchronous prescaler from it (0x7F for LSE, 0x7C for LSI) and bms_rtc_wakeup_period_set picks the wake-up counter scale from it. Only 0 or 1.

bms_g_4168_20000692.name: bms_rtc_lse_timeout
bms_g_4168_20000692.description: Timeout result of the clock start-up polls. 1 when the wait loop for LSERDY or LSIRDY ran out (the loop counter passed 0x87FFF, about 0x88000 iterations), 0 when it did not. bms_rtc_select_lse_and_start and bms_rtc_clock_bringup store the result, bms_rtc_select_lse_and_start clears it before it starts, and bms_rtc_fallback_lsi_start sets it to 1 when it moves to the LSI source. Only 0 or 1.

bms_g_4168_20000694.name: bms_rtc_lse_timeout_copy
bms_g_4168_20000694.description: Copy of the timeout flag at 0x20000692, taken inside bms_rtc_fallback_lsi_start just before that flag is set to 1 for the LSI fallback. It keeps the LSE or LSI wait result after the flag is overwritten, probably for diagnostics. Only 0 or 1.

bms_g_4168_20001c80.name: bms_rtc_snapshot_tick
bms_g_4168_20001c80.description: Time-base stamp taken by bms_rtc_reset_with_snapshot when it resets the RTC backup domain and restarts LSE. The value is the 32-bit time base returned by bms_tick_get (0x20000678). Its unit is the unit of that time base, which is not known from this packet. Written only in bms_rtc_reset_with_snapshot here.

bms_g_4168_20001c84.name: bms_rtc_snapshot_record
bms_g_4168_20001c84.description: Four-byte bit-packed date and time record. bms_rtc_datetime_pack fills it from the RTC calendar in binary form, bms_rtc_reset_with_snapshot and bms_rtc_timestamp_record_start store snapshots here, and bms_packed_datetime_shift_seconds shifts it in place by a number of seconds. The bit fields are only partly decoded (day, month and weekday from bms_rtc_datetime_pack; seconds, minutes, hours, day, month and year minus 2000 from bms_packed_datetime_shift_seconds). Not reset by the routines in this packet.

bms_g_4168_20001c8a.name: bms_seq_substate
bms_g_4168_20001c8a.description: Sub-state index shared by the RTC snapshot routines and the fault record service. bms_seq_state_reset clears it, bms_nibble_debounce_1s sets it to 1 or 2, bms_rtc_timestamp_record_start sets it to 2 and bms_rtc_reset_with_snapshot sets it to 3. bms_fault_record_service uses it as the index into the handler table at 0x080108A8, and bms_flag_20001c8a_is_clear reports whether it is 0. Range 0 to 3 as seen here.

bms_g_4168_20005d00.name: bms_rtc_handle
bms_g_4168_20005d00.description: RTC peripheral handle in the HAL layout, filled by bms_rtc_hal_init and used by the HAL RTC calls (init, get and set date and time, wake-up enable and disable) and by the RTC and tamper interrupt vector, which passes its address on. The field layout is described in the RtcHandle struct; only the fields written here are identified. The handle may be larger than the 40 bytes described here.

bms_g_4168_20005d48.name: bms_rtc_epoch_tm
bms_g_4168_20005d48.description: Broken-down time output of bms_epoch_to_tm, which converts a Unix epoch in seconds into this record. The wrapper bms_epoch_to_tm_20005d48 passes this address as the output. bms_packed_datetime_shift_seconds uses it to convert a packed date and time after adding an offset in seconds.
